cover.headline: **A fact costs work to create**, and past a critical angle no energy can make it objective.

slides.title: Recording an event so it becomes objective fact has a thermodynamic price that scales with redundancy.
slides.body:
The team computed the minimum work to create records at different levels of redundancy. Beyond a critical misalignment angle, they report objectivity becomes unreachable at any energy cost.

This links the emergence of classical facts to energy and entropy, not just information.

slides.title: Work required to create one event record scaled linearly with redundancy at the Landauer coefficient.
slides.body:
The model used a central qubit writing to N thermal registers. Work needed was at least R times Boltzmann constant times temperature times a function of error rate.

Erasing accessed records yielded net work gain beyond the first copy.

slides.title: The team modeled a driven qubit broadcasting records into registers with work sources and thermal baths.
slides.body:
They calculated exact thermodynamic costs for creating, keeping, and destroying records in this minimal broadcast model. They derived closed-form expressions for optimal work in the pointer basis.

They also computed power needed to maintain a record as a nonequilibrium steady state.

caveats: This is a preprint. It has not been peer reviewed yet, so no independent expert has checked the work.
This is a theoretical model with idealized conditions. Real physical systems may behave differently from the minimal broadcast setup used here.

source.abstract: An event becomes a fact when enough independent records of it exist such that no operation is possible that leaves all observers ignorant of it again. Records are physical, and creating, keeping, and destroying them have thermodynamic costs. We compute these costs exactly in a minimal broadcast model with a driven central qubit writing records into $N$ initially thermal registers, with work sources and baths at temperature $T$. The basic arguments for the operations are outlined here, with full treatment in the text. Creation of one event record at redundancy $R$ and information deficit $δ$ requires work $W \ge R\, k_\mathrm{B}T \ln 2\, (1-δ) H(\varepsilon)$, linear in redundancy at the Landauer coefficient. Recording in a basis misaligned by $θ$ with the einselecting interaction fails at a critical angle, $θ_c = 2\arcsin\sqrt{H_2^{-1}(δ)}$, beyond which objectivity is unreachable at any work, and below $θ_c$ the optimal work is a closed form in the pointer basis that minimizes the work of objectivity. Reducing objectivity is impossible at any work with access to fewer than $R - R_{\min} + 1$ records, while work protects nothing if given access. Inter-record redundancy is extractable free energy and erasing the accessed records yields a net gain of work beyond the first copy. The second law constrains the destruction of the correlation: erasing a fact from a sector an adversary controls dissipates at least the mutual information erased, but a consolidation dissipates nothing. Records in re-thermalizing media are nonequilibrium steady states, and the minimal power to maintain a record at $(R,δ)$ is the known two-state driving bound evaluated at the record-quality boundary.
